description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Sen. Rick Scott (R-FL) discusses the ongoing negotiations between the US and Iran, the blowback on President Trump's 'weaponization' fund, as well as the Texas Republican runoff election. Michael Allen, Beacon Global Strategies Managing Director, speaks on the situation in the Middle East and how the handling of the conflict may reflect on President Trump and his allies in time. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Texas Showdown Latest Test of Trump's Sway | Balance of Power: Late Edition 5/26/2026

description: Senator Rick Scott (R-FL), a member of the Senate Foreign Relations and Armed Services Committees, says he would be “shocked” if President Trump agreed to delay the nuclear component of any Iran deal, warning the choice is “unbelievable hostilities or a deal” and saying more military strikes may be needed to eliminate Iran’s nuclear capability. He also backs Trump’s proposed weaponization fund while saying he won’t seek taxpayer compensation himself, predicts Raúl Castro will leave Cuba before the US “pick[s] him up,” and says Republicans will hold Texas despite the bruising Cornyn-Paxton primary. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Sen. Scott: Trump Won’t Punt Iran Nuclear Demands

author: Nicola M White
description: The Securities and Exchange Commission is mulling changes to decades-old rules that prohibit companies from certain communications during the going-public process, as the Wall Street regulator looks to boost initial public offerings.
title: SEC Chairman Eyes ‘Gun-Jumping’ Rule Changes to Spur More IPOs

description: Michael Allen, Beacon Global Strategies Managing Director, says President Trump and his team have a decreasing number of options to secure a deal with Iran, citing concerns that any agreement could be vague and may not deliver the concessions the US needs. Allen also says Operation Epic Fury and the subsequent conflict could end up being a strategic loss for the United States if the US is unable to reopen or neutralize the Strait. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Michael Allen: 'Decreasing Number of Options' on Iran

author: Alex Wickham
description: The UK and other western nations are running out of time to maintain their technological edge over China, the UK’s top cyber spy is set to warn Wednesday, urging businesses to work with intelligence officials in order to stay ahead.
title: UK Spy Chief Warns China Is Closing Cyber Gap With West

author: Beatriz Reis, Matheus Piovesana
description: Brazil’s Finance ministry signaled that it will help strengthen the regional bank controlled by the nation’s capital city after the lender was hurt by the fallout from the failure of Banco Master SA.
title: Brazil Signals It Will Ease Rules to Bolster Brasilia’s Bank

author: Alicia Diaz
description: US Trade Ambassador Jamieson Greer said his agency will issue a notice in the Federal Register “shortly” to seek public comments on a Board of Trade with China, a formal step to establish a new mechanism to manage economic relations between the countries.
title: US Says Process to Form China Board of Trade to Start Shortly

author: Joe Mayes
description: The UK is poised to sign a new defense and security pact with Poland, as the NATO allies seek to curb the threat posed by Russia.
title: UK, Poland Sign Defense and Security Pact to Curb Russia Threat

author: Daniel Carvalho
description: President Donald Trump met Tuesday with Flávio Bolsonaro, the top challenger to leftist incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Brazil’s looming presidential election.
title: Trump Meets Brazil Candidate Flávio Bolsonaro at White House

author: Lucy White
description: Former Labour Prime Minister Tony Blair criticized the party he once led for “playing with fire” in its attempt to oust current premier Keir Starmer, while also slamming the government for lacking a clear agenda.
title: Ex-UK Premier Tony Blair Lambastes Labour’s Leadership Woes

author: David Gura, Rachael Lewis-Krisky
description: Can Cuba withstand mounting US pressure? On the Big Take: the campaign to cripple Cuba’s government and why US intervention in Venezuela may be a blueprint for Havana’s future.
title: What Trump’s Venezuela Blueprint Means for Cuba

author: Nancy Cook
description: Trump-backed Paxton is facing off against incumbent Cornyn in a runoff.
title: Texas Republicans Make Their Choice in Bitter Senate Contest

description: Today, Chris Kennedy, Bloomberg Economics lead on economic statecraft, breaks down the latest in negotiations between the US and Iran as the two sides traded renewed strikes over the weekend. Then, Peter Atwater, president of Financial Insyghts, discusses the 'K-shaped economy' as war fueled inflation squeezes consumers across the US. Plus, Louise Phillips Forbes discusses New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's proposed pied-a-terre tax and what it could mean for the real estate market. Finally, Michael Swanson, chief agriculture economist at Wells Fargo's Agri-Food Institute, talks the impact of supply chain disruption and higher fuel prices on farmers and consumers at the grocery store and at the dinner table. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Consumer Confidence Slips on Price Concerns| Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 5/26/2026

author: Naomi Ng, Rebecca Choong Wilkins
description: On the Big Take Asia podcast: What it takes to feed tens of millions of Indonesians and why Prabowo’s signature program is under pressure.
title: Why Indonesia’s $15 Billion Free Lunch Program Is Unnerving Investors

description: A landmark ruling recognizing Indigenous rights over 800 acres of metro Vancouver has triggered political upheaval in Canada. The government now must reconcile Aboriginal title with existing owners. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Canada’s Legal Fight Over Indigenous Lands

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss peace negotiations between the US and Iran. On today's show, former State Department official Heather Conley, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, BGR Group Principal Lester Munson, Lockheed Martin President Tim Cahill and Texas Politics Project Director James Henson. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Touts Iran Deal Prospects | Balance of Power: Early Edition 5/26/2026

author: Sotiris Nikas
description: Former Greek Prime Minister Alexis Tsipras announced the formation of a new party, adding to the country’s fragmented political landscape as it enters an election year.
title: Former Greek Premier Tsipras Forms New Party Ahead of Election

description: Peter Atwater, president at Financial Insyghts and lecturer at William & Mary College, said that the top and bottom of the 'K-shaped economy' have become two vastly different experiences with 'nothing in common' as consumers on the bottom leg of the 'K' feel the daily impact of war fueled inflation and a labor market impacted by AI. Atwater says that the affordability crunch at the bottom of the 'K' will likely result in political turnover in midterm elections this fall.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Outlook for Future is 'Divided' Between Sides of 'K-Shaped' Economy, Says Peter Atwater

description: China’s Greater Bay Area will fuse 11 cities into a megalopolis that includes Hong Kong, which Beijing hopes will become a new Silicon Valley. But the plan is part of a much larger transformation. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: China’s Plans for an Urban Super City

description: James Henson, Director of the Texas Politics Project at the University of Texas at Austin said that if the TX GOP primary was going to come down money. Sen. John Cornyn (R-TX) would be "running away" with the race.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Texas’ Cornyn-Paxton Fracas Concludes After $130M in Ads

author: Alexandra Samuels, Greg Giroux
description: The South Carolina Senate nixed a proposal backed by President Donald Trump to enact more Republican-friendly congressional lines for the 2026 election.
title: South Carolina Republicans Fail to Advance Map Targeting Clyburn

author: Jasmina Kuzmanovic
description: Croatia is seriously considering Ante Zigman to head its central bank, according to a person familiar with the government’s thinking.
title: Croatia Seriously Considering Zigman as New Central Bank Chief

description:
Heather Conley, Nonresident Senior Fellow at AEI and Former Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for the Bureau of European and Eurasian Affairs says because Iran controls the Strait of Hormuz, they have a strategic advantage. 

 (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Touts Iran Deal Prospects

author: Magdalena Del Valle
description: China’s top diplomat made thinly veiled jabs at President Donald Trump’s foreign policy from the United Nations, using an address to criticize the US war on Iran and the administration’s approach to the global organization.
title: China’s Top Diplomat Makes Veiled Jabs at Trump From UN

description: Tim Cahill, Lockheed Martin president for missiles and fire control, says the company will quadruple production of THAAD interceptors out of a facility in Troy, Alabama. He says the contractor is working with the Pentagon and suppliers to rapidly resupply the US stockpile of missiles. He speaks on "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Lockheed Moving Rapidly to Resupply US Missile Stockpile

author: Miranda Davis
description: President Donald Trump took aim at Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson and Illinois Governor JB Pritzker, calling them “terrible” and saying they should ask for assistance after a driver injured five police officers who were responding to a so-called teen takeover over the weekend.
title: Trump Lashes Out at Chicago After ‘Teen Takeover’ Hurts Officers

author: Jim Wyss
description: The head of Puerto Rico’s economic development department and about a dozen others quit their posts Tuesday, complicating some of the government’s key initiatives that aim to attract manufacturing and wealthy mainlanders to the US territory.
title: Puerto Rico’s Economic Chief, Key Staff Members Quit

author: Courtney McBride
description: The US is touting progress toward a peace deal with Iran to end the nearly three-month war, even amid fresh hostilities and uncertainty over the vital Strait of Hormuz.
title: US Touts Iran Deal Prospects Amid Fresh Tensions in Hormuz

author: Brian Platt
description: Canada is set to announce a deal to supply Germany with liquefied natural gas from a planned export facility on the coast of British Columbia, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Germany, Canada to Sign Major LNG Deal as Europe Seeks Energy Security

author: Kevin Crowley, Jennifer A Dlouhy, Fabiola Zerpa, David Wethe
description: Exxon Mobil Corp. and ConocoPhillips are pushing for durable contract terms and a way to resolve billions of dollars owed to them as they consider re-entering Venezuela after exiting the country two decades ago.
title: Exxon, ConocoPhillips Seek Safeguards to Return to Venezuela

description: The intense Republican primary runoff election for a US Senate seat from Texas comes to an end today. The showdown between incumbent John Cornyn and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has become one the most expensive in Senate history. Joe Lovinger reports.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Nasty Texas Republican Runoff Comes to a Head Today

author: Kate Sullivan, Catherine Lucey
description: President Donald Trump said his physical at Walter Reed National Military Medical Center went “PERFECTLY,” but provided no details on the results of his examination.
title: Trump Says Medical Exam Went Well But Provides No Details

author: Gregory Korte
description: The Trump administration is moving to create a government-wide nondisclosure agreement for federal workers after a number of high-profile and unauthorized leaks in recent months.
title: Trump Administration Demands Federal Worker NDAs in New Crackdown on Leaks

author: Alastair Reed
description: Scotland’s devolved parliament voted to demand the UK government hand over the power to hold a fresh independence referendum as First Minister John Swinney seeks to build on a recent election win and take advantage of political turmoil in London.
title: Scotland Renews Push for Independence With Labour in Turmoil

author: Dan Strumpf, Eric Martin, Sudhi Ranjan Sen
description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s four-day visit to India featured warm handshakes and promises of deeper cooperation. There was even a surprise call by President Donald Trump to a US embassy-sponsored bash in New Delhi, where he told guests how much he loved the country.
title: Rubio Seeks to Repair US-India Relations After Trump-Era Strains

author: Dan Williams
description: Israel’s military said its ground forces are moving further into Lebanon, in what could signal an expanded presence in the south of the country as part of the ongoing war with Iran-backed Hezbollah.
title: Israeli Troops Push Further Into Lebanon in War With Hezbollah

description:
US and Iranian forces clashed near the Strait of Hormuz overnight, highlighting the tension between the two sides even as they tout progress toward an interim peace deal.

The exchange of strikes came hours after US President Donald Trump said negotiations with Tehran to extend their ceasefire and reopen the strait are proceeding, though Secretary of State Marco Rubio added Tuesday that a deal would likely take a few days to finalize.

For more on the state of the conflict, we speak with Ret. Adm. James Stavridis, Bloomberg Opinion contributor and former Supreme Allied Commander of NATO. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: James Stavridis: Chokepoint Economy Starts With Hormuz

author: Lucca de Paoli, Donal Griffin
description: Cryptocurrency firm HTX has been sanctioned by the UK government, who allege that the exchange was part of “infrastructure” used by Russia to circumvent sanctions and allegedly move $1.5 billion back to the Kremlin.
title: Crypto Firm HTX Sanctioned by UK for Helping Kremlin Move Money

author: Patrick Sykes
description: The US and Iran have been locked in a stalemate since agreeing to a ceasefire in April. They’ve been unable to reach a deal to end a monthslong war that has killed thousands of people and sparked a global energy crunch.
title: The Key Sticking Points for a US-Iran Peace Deal

author: Milda Seputyte
description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called for unified alert systems and improved cross-border coordination after a string of Ukrainian drone incursions into Baltic airspace exposed gaps in Europe’s defenses.
title: EU Seeks to Fix Baltic Defense Gaps After Drone Incursions

author: Zijia Song
description: Bolivian sovereign bonds are in free-fall, dropping for a 10th day on Tuesday as protests and road blockades choke off essential supplies to La Paz and lead to violent clashes, threatening to push South America’s poorest country back into political and economic chaos.
title: Bolivia Unrest Threatens Return of Chaos, Sinks Sovereign Bonds

author: Carolina Gonzalez
description: Chile’s new government said it’s facing a steeper fiscal challenge than even it had anticipated, claiming the previous administration of President Gabriel Boric had overestimated revenue and turned a blind eye to some expenses.
title: Chile’s New Government Cries Foul Over Past Debt Projections

author: Greg Stohr
description: The US Supreme Court refused to let Florida file an unusual lawsuit that accused California and Washington of making it too easy for undocumented immigrants to get commercial driver’s licenses.
title: Supreme Court Ducks State Clash Over Immigrant Driver’s Licenses

author: Patrick Van Oosterom
description: The Dutch government blocked a proposed takeover of Solvinity Group BV, a provider of cloud services in the Netherlands, by US-based Kyndryl, citing security concerns.
title: Dutch Block US Takeover of Cloud Services Provider Solvinity

author: Aliaksandr Kudrytski
description: With the battlefield largely at a stalemate, Russia is ramping up ballistic missile attacks on Ukraine to try to regain the strategic initiative by overwhelming air defenses and demoralizing its population.
title: Putin Steps Up Kyiv Missile Strikes Seeking New Momentum in War

author: Anthony Halpin
description: The Kremlin said Alexander Shokhin, head of the lobby group representing major industries in Russia, will become President Vladimir Putin’s new business ombudsman.
title: Kremlin Names Top Business Lobby Chief as Putin’s New Ombudsman

description: The US, Japan, India and Australia launched a maritime surveillance initiative for the Indo-Pacific region as the Hormuz crisis deepens. Debjit Chakraborty explains how the high-profile summit aims to counter growing threats to commerce. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rubio Unveils Indo-Pacific Monitor Plan as Hormuz Crisis Deepens

description: US and Iranian forces clashed near the Strait of Hormuz overnight, even as they tout progress toward an interim peace deal. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fresh Clashes Highlight US-Iran Tensions Despite Talks Progress

author: Matheus Piovesana, Daniel Carvalho
description: Brazil’s federal police carried out search-and-seizure warrants against former Rio de Janeiro Governor Cláudio Castro as part of a new phase of the investigation into failed lender Banco Master SA.
title: Brazil Police Raid Ex-Rio Governor’s Home in Banco Master Probe

author: Greg Giroux
description: The runoff pits a longstanding GOP senator against a Trump-backed ‘fighter’
title: Texas Senate Showdown Latest Test of Trump’s Sway

author: Alessandra Migliaccio
description: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni accused the European Union of restricting the bloc’s ability to grow and be competitive on the world stage.
title: Italy’s Meloni Says EU Bureaucrats Stifle Economic Growth

description: Beijing’s close ties with Pakistan help it influence negotiations to end the Iran war.
title: China Plays Quiet Role in US-Iran Talks

author: Martha Viotti Beck, Barbara Nascimento
description: When President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s senior officials convene on Mondays to discuss Brazil’s most pressing government business, one rule is clear: keep quiet if you’re not advocating for stimulus.
title: President Lula’s Stimulus Machine Is Steamrolling Brazil’s Sky-High Interest Rates

author: Andre-Pierre Du Plessis
description: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa filed court papers seeking a review of an independent panel’s report that suggested he may have broken the law in his handling of the theft of foreign exchange hidden in a sofa at his wildlife ranch in 2020.
title: S. Africa President Files Papers Contesting Cash-in-Sofa Report

author: Katarina Hoije
description: Senegal’s parliament reinstated Ousmane Sonko as a lawmaker on Tuesday, paving the way for his likely election as speaker of the National Assembly days after President Bassirou Diomaye Faye abruptly dismissed him as prime minister in a split that has fractured the ruling coalition.
title: Senegal’s Sonko Returns to Parliament, Set to Lead Assembly

author: Nancy Cook
description: Republican voters in Texas get their final say Tuesday in a drawn out, vitriolic and expensive primary campaign for a US Senate seat, a race that Democrats are watching closely in hopes that they could flip both houses of Congress in November.
title: Texas Voters Get Final Say After Trump Backs Paxton in Runoff

author: Patrick Sykes
description: Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said US military bases in the Middle East will no longer be safe after the war, declaring victory and a new regional order even as talks to end the conflict continued.
title: Iran’s Khamenei Says No Going Back For Middle East Rocked by War

author: Arsalan Shahla, Alisa Odenheimer
description: US and Iranian forces clashed near the Strait of Hormuz overnight, highlighting the tension between the two sides even as they tout progress toward an interim peace deal.
title: US and Iran Clash Near Hormuz Even as Both Tout Talks Progress

author: Charlie Zhu
description: China is restricting overseas travel for top AI professionals in private firms such as Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. and DeepSeek, suggesting an escalation in measures intended to safeguard its technology and catch up to the US in a pivotal sphere.
title: China Expands Travel Curbs to Top AI Talent at Private Firms

author: Yoshiaki Nohara
description: Japan has sent senior officials to Russia to keep communication channels open and protect the assets of Japanese companies operating there, in what Tokyo says is the latest in a series of visits that have taken place since the war in Ukraine began.
title: Japan Sends Officials to Russia to ‘Facilitate Communication’

author: Seyoon Kim
description: North Korea fired multiple projectiles including short-range ballistic missiles on Tuesday, South Korea’s military said, the latest in a series of weapons tests by Pyongyang so far this year.
title: North Korea Fires Ballistic Missiles in Latest Weapons Test

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

US and Israeli jets struck Iranian vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and other targets, hours after President Donald Trump had suggested negotiations with Tehran over an interim deal were progressing.

The attack took place south of Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, with several Iranian personnel killed, Iran’s state-run Nour News reported, without providing further details. Trump earlier said negotiations between the US and Iran over an agreement to extend their ceasefire and reopen the strait were “proceeding nicely.”

Today's guest: Shriya Samarth, StoneX, EMEA Head of Rates. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Strikes Iran as Trump Says Talks 'Proceeding Nicely' | Daybreak Europe 05/26/2026

author: Katarina Hoije
description: Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye named a veteran economist and former central banker as his new prime minister, shoring up his economic team ahead of the restart of talks with the International Monetary Fund on a new funding program.
title: Ex-Central Banker Named as Senegal’s Premier Ahead of IMF Talks

author: Saikat Das, Siddhi Nayak
description: The Reserve Bank of India has held discussions with local credit-rating companies to gauge potential stress among borrowers caused by the US-Iran war, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: RBI, Rating Firms Assess Iran War Risks on Indian Companies

description: US and Israeli jets struck Iranian vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and other targets, hours after President Donald Trump had suggested negotiations with Tehran over an interim deal were progressing. Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche has the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Strikes Iran Targets as Trump Hails Progress on Talks

author: Heesu Lee
description: South Korea unveiled a roadmap to develop nuclear-powered submarines and deploy the first vessel by the late 2030s, as President Lee Jae Myung convened a new defense strategy council Tuesday focused on strengthening the nation’s military autonomy.
title: S. Korea to Deploy Locally Built Nuclear Submarine by Late-2030s

description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov advised US State Secretary Marco Rubio to evacuate US citizens and diplomats from Kyiv, as the Kremlin plans to continue heavy strikes on the Ukrainian capital, according to a statement published by the Russian Foreign Ministry Monday. Bloomberg's Anthony Halpin reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Russia Tells US to Evacuate Citizens, Diplomats From Kyiv

author: Daniel Basteiro
description: When Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez overturned a significant polling deficit to hold on to power in 2023, his Socialist predecessor José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero was a crucial ally on the campaign trail. Three years later, Zapatero’s legal troubles are threatening the Socialist leader’s bid for reelection next year.
title: This Spanish Graft Probe Really Hurts the Sánchez Government

author: Josh Xiao, Andrea Tan, Alfred Cang
description: China’s top military official is expected to skip Asia’s biggest defense forum for a second year in a row, according to people familiar with the matter, ceding to the US and its allies an opportunity for public defense diplomacy.
title: China Defense Minister Expected to Skip Singapore Forum Again

author: Nariman Gizitdinov
description: Kazakhstan’s national railroad operator is expanding its track and infrastructure to meet growing demand for transporting goods between China and Europe as trade flows shift in response to the Iran war.
title: Iran War Boosts $10 Billion Kazakh Rail Plan Linking EU to China

author: Philip Heijmans
description: Singapore’s top diplomat is making a rare visit to North Korea as part of a regional tour that includes stops in China and South Korea as the city-state seeks to boost diplomatic engagement amid intensifying geopolitical tensions.
title: Singapore’s Top Envoy Heads to North Korea in Rare Visit

author: Sudhi Ranjan Sen, Sakura Murakami
description: Foreign ministers from the US, Japan, India and Australia are meeting in New Delhi as the Quad grouping seeks to revive momentum after a high-profile clash between President Donald Trump and Indian leader Narendra Modi.
title: Quad Diplomats Meet in India to Revive Group After Trump Tension

author: Arsalan Shahla
description: Iran’s government could soon roll back some restrictions on a months-long digital blackout that has cut off millions of its citizens from the internet, the official Islamic Republic News Agency said, as diplomatic talks between the US and Tehran gather pace.
title: Iran Signals Potential Easing of Internet Blackout Amid US Talks
